subject.title: Control UI: Config upgrade/hardening suggestions should apply changes automatically with before/after diff and user acceptance, not direct users to edit files manually

question: Which Control UI auth, hardening, and compatibility recommendations may be applied automatically from the browser, and what diff, confirmation, allowlist, audit, and rollback policy must gate them?
rationale: The remaining work persists security and auth-related config from a browser-visible UI, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary or the set of safe mutations.

options.title: Define Allowlisted Recommendation Actions
options.body: Create a generic allowlisted UI action model that reuses config.patch/config.apply validation and shows exact diff, confirmation, dismissal, restart/audit, and redaction behavior for approved recommendations.

options.title: Keep Risky Auth Changes Manual
options.body: Leave auth/security downgrade or recovery suggestions as manual guidance while allowing only low-risk non-auth recommendations to become one-click actions.

options.title: Split By Recommendation Class
options.body: Use separate policies for hardening, compatibility, and recovery recommendations so secure-by-default changes can be one-click while downgrade paths require stronger consent.

recommendation.title: Define Allowlisted Recommendation Actions
recommendation.body: Create a generic allowlisted UI action model that reuses config.patch/config.apply validation and shows exact diff, confirmation, dismissal, restart/audit, and redaction behavior for approved recommendations.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest observed connection across Control UI settings, config validation/restart safety, and security-sensitive product direction.
